newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end up, spot down.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end up, spot down.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed mostly up on Tuesday, with institutions borrowing money on the market to trade three new domestic A shares to be listed tomorrow, traders said.
The annual rate for the most active three-day contract soared to 24.05 percent from 17.00 percent on Monday.
Total turnover rose to 11.04 million lots from nearly ten million. One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
"The rates, in particular those for the early-maturing contracts, were pushed sharply up today by the forthcoming listing of three new A shares," one trader said.
The issue of Xinhua Department Co today also helped to boost the rates, traders said. They expect rates to move around current levels tomorrow.
Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended mostly down on rumours that the Finance Ministry will shortly announce a quota for next year's state debt issue, traders said.
The most active 10-year bond that matures in June 2006 ended down at 115.65 yuan from 115.81 yuan.
Combined volume of the nine-contract market rose to 898,514 lots from 882,847 lots.
Traders said the 1997 state debt issue quota was expected to be a record 250 billion yuan, which was likely to attract liquidity away from the T-bill spot market.
"If the rumours prove to be true, the spot contracts will continue to fall in the short term," said one trader.
